Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers arriving illegally. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences. A 20% National Insurance rate would apply to foreign workers (exempting healthcare workers and small businesses), with proceeds funding apprenticeships. Student visa rules would bar dependents, and a 5-year residency requirement would apply before claiming benefits.

## Economy
Personal tax changes include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 (removing 7 million people from income tax), cutting stamp duty (0% below £750k), abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and reducing fuel duty by 20p per litre. For businesses, corporation tax would drop to 15% by year three, the VAT threshold would rise to £150,000, IR35 rules would be abolished, and business rates eliminated for high street SMEs while introducing a 4% online delivery tax for large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed savings include stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion annually), requiring 5% efficiency savings across departments (£50 billion), halving foreign aid (£6 billion saved), and improving HMRC tax collection.

## NHS
Frontline NHS staff would pay zero basic rate tax for three years. The party proposes 20% tax relief on private healthcare, an NHS voucher scheme allowing private treatment if waiting time targets are missed, and expanded use of independent healthcare providers. A public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms is proposed.

## Energy
Net Zero commitments would be scrapped, along with renewable energy subsidies. The party would fast-track North Sea oil and gas licences, grant shale gas test licences, and develop small modular nuclear reactors.

## Policing and Justice
Plans include recruiting 40,000 new frontline officers over five years, implementing zero-tolerance policing, increasing stop and search, and building 10,000 new detention places. Mandatory life sentences would apply for violent repeat offenders. Child grooming would become an aggravating offence with deportation for dual citizens.

## Education
Proposals include curriculum changes requiring balanced teaching of historical topics, banning gender transitioning discussions in schools, 20% tax relief on independent school fees, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers.

## Benefits
The income tax threshold increase aims to incentivise work. A "2-strike rule" would withdraw benefits after two refused job offers. Face-to-face assessments would replace remote evaluations.

## Defence
Spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with a pay review for armed forces personnel, a dedicated veterans ministry, and recruitment of 30,000 full-time army personnel.

## Housing and Infrastructure
Planning reforms would fast-track brownfield development. Social housing would prioritise local residents. HS2 would be scrapped. ULEZ zones and low traffic neighbourhoods would be banned. A new ownership model would bring 50% of utilities into public ownership.

## Constitutional Changes
Proposals include leaving the ECHR, reforming the House of Lords, restricting postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation. The BBC licence fee would be scrapped.

## Funding
Total projected savings: £150 billion annually, plus £10 billion from assumed additional economic growth. Total projected costs: £141 billion annually.
